body.x: JD Sound (President Hans Kim, www.jdsound.co.kr) presented Monster GODJ, a portable DJ system, at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

Monster GODJ is the world’s first DJ instrument to have dual touchpad LCDs, and its numerous features add to the analog sentiments as well as extreme convenience. At 300g, weighing about two smartphones put together, this portable DJ system offers quality music creations at clubs and parties.

The product is able to play incessantly for up to 12 hours. Music that has already been played can be edited to created something new, and its demonstration is possible anywhere, anytime. The dual touchpad turntables along with built-in 16 beat sequencers, 8 music pads, various sound effects, automated functions, and 3-band equalizer all provide means to easily create various types of music.
Additionally, headphones, Amp speakers, and microphones can be used simply by connecting to line-in and line-out, while the product can also be linked to Android smartphones and tablet PCs.
JD Sound is an audio-specialty company with audio platform skills. It is internationally distributing the world’s first portable and independent DJ instrument.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
